transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Tara Li (HelioPay), Samir Kapoor (HelioPay), Lina Gomez (HelioPay), Ravi Menon (HelioPay)

Summary (auto): Integration discovery covering SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway proxying, quotas, and observability. Customer leaning private/dedicated due to data residency and compliance; wants clarity on integration effort and throttling behavior.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros, we'll mostly cover how Redwood would fit into HelioPay's stack — SDKs, langchain adapters, and the gateway story.
[01:00] Tara: Thanks, Aisha. high level — we need to understand if we can start on hosted and later move to private/dedicated without major code changes. Also curious about rate limits per-tenant.
[02:00] Miguel (SE): totally. For most customers the integration surface is our HTTP SDKs (python/node/go) and we provide official LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors that map the chain abstractions to Redwood endpoints. code changes are usually minimal — swap client, minimal config.
[03:00] Samir: can you clarify the LangChain adapter? we use LangChain heavily in our orchestration layer, and some teams use LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation.
[04:00] Miguel (SE): sure — the adapter implements the LLM and Chat classes, so calls look like standard LangChain LLMChain calls. we also expose streaming websocket support for token-by-token responses which LangChain can consume. LlamaIndex connectors map to our embeddings endpoint; you just point the index to the Redwood embeddings client.
[05:00] Ravi: how about auth — our infra uses an internal gateway/proxy, we need to keep API keys off client devices. recommended pattern?
[06:00] Aisha (AE): common pattern is to have your gateway inject a short-lived token or proxy requests from backend services. Redwood supports per-key quotas and route-based policies so you can attach a key to a tenant and let the gateway do routing.
[07:00] Lina (Security): on that, what logs do we get? we need audit trails for PII touches and KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
[08:00] Miguel (SE): we provide audit logs, request/response metadata (note: bodies may be redacted depending on retention settings). For Private deployments we support bringing your own KMS/HSM. Hosted also supports KMS integrations for encryption-at-rest but BYOK for private.
[09:00] Tara: does the hosted product support SSO for consoles and RBAC for keys? we have separate tenant admins.
[10:00] Aisha: yes — SAML SSO for console, RBAC at organization and route levels, and per-key scoping. we'll share the SOC2 and SSO docs in the pack.
[11:00] Miguel (SE): wanted to touch on quotas — Redwood lets you set global and per-key rate limits and token quotas. enforcement can be at gateway level or inside our runtime. for dedicated deployments you get more granular control (e.g., per-queue).
[12:00] Samir: how deterministic is throttling? we have bursty traffic around payroll runs, so we need predictable fallback behaviors.
[13:00] Miguel: you can configure burst windows and queuing policies. also Redwood can route to lower-capacity model variants automatically when capacity is constrained — that's a circuit-breaker style fallback.
[14:00] Tara: model variants — would that change latency much? our UX needs sub-300ms token latency for short prompts.
[15:00] Miguel: sub-300ms is possible on dedicated with optimized kernels and batching tuned to your seq lengths. hosted can hit similar numbers for small models but dedicated is more predictable. we'll need to run benchmarks with your prompt distribution.
[16:00] Ravi: about the gateway — we currently run an Envoy layer that does tenant routing. is there anything special we should configure to preserve streaming semantics?
[17:00] Miguel: ensure HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 passthrough for streaming responses and avoid buffering proxies that reassemble bodies. Envoy config with grpc or raw streaming is fine; we'll share a sample config.
[18:00] Lina (Security): retention and redaction — can we set per-tenant retention windows and auto-redact responses containing SSNs or card numbers?
[19:00] Miguel: we have retention policies by workspace and optional scrubbers. auto-detection can be tuned, though for strict PII you should handle redaction at the gateway before sending. for private you can disable retention entirely.
[20:00] Aisha: quick note — many fintechs start on hosted for dev and move to dedicated/private for production and compliance. the API surface remains the same so most code is portable.
[21:00] Samir: how do we instrument observability? we use Datadog and Prometheus — want traces, per-request metadata, and token-level cost breakdowns in our dashboards.
[22:00] Miguel: Redwood emits metrics via Prometheus and we have traces that include request id, model, token counts, and latency. we can ship logs to your S3 or push to Datadog. token-level cost is available in per-request metadata so you can aggregate in your dashboards.
[23:00] Tara: any pre-built tracing hooks for OpenTelemetry?
[24:00] Miguel: yes we provide an OpenTelemetry integration that adds spans around LLM calls and includes attributes for model, prompt id, and cache hits. we'll include the OTEL example in the repo.
[25:00] Ravi: about caching — you mentioned KV cache earlier. how transparent is prefix caching for us? we have repeated prompts across sessions.
[26:00] Miguel: runtime-level KV caching benefits prompt prefixes; it's transparent to the SDK. you can also configure application-level caching via response hashes. for embeddings we have a vector cache for repeated queries.
[27:00] Lina: encryption key lifecycle — for hosted if we integrate with our KMS are keys rotated automatically or do we manage rotation?
[28:00] Miguel: if you bring your KMS we can either manage rotations via customer policies or you can rotate and push new keys, depending on the integration. we'll circle the exact supported KMS vendors in the pack.
[29:00] Samir: what's the effort to switch from hosted to dedicated? downtime, code differences?
[30:00] Aisha: practically none on code — mostly config and capacity planning. we help with the migration: export keys, set up routes, and schedule a cutover. some customers run a canary for a week.
[31:00] Miguel: technically dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and custom autoscaling policies. private gives you control over VPC and audit endpoints.
[32:00] Tara: licensing and pricing — can we get an example for a 2-year dedicated commit vs hosted usage?
[33:00] Aisha: yes we'll share model: hosted per-token plus subscription add-ons; dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits. I'll include a templated pricing sheet after this call.
[34:00] Ravi: on rate limits — can rules be dynamic per-route? e.g., stricter for production routes and looser for internal dev keys?
[35:00] Miguel: yes, route-based policies allow different qps and token quotas; you can attach policies to keys. rules can be updated via API and take effect quickly.
[36:00] Lina: one last sec — for compliance we'll need an architectural diagram showing data flows and where tokens are stored.
[37:00] Aisha: we'll include an architecture diagram in the security pack and propose next steps: security pack, a sample-run benchmark, and an SE deep dive.
[38:05] Aisha: great, thanks all. we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. end.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — speaker labels sometimes generic; some technical terms like KV cache, LlamaIndex spelled in different ways in parts of the transcript. references shared: security pack link (sent post-call), sample Envoy config (link), LangChain adapter repo (link)
